title: Optimize evals 1:1 prep - quality regressions & A/B review
content:
Meeting: Optimize / Evals review (prep for 1:1 with Matt)
Date: 2026-03-04 (sync)
Attendees (planned): Lena, Matt, Jamie (opt), Aisha (evals)
Objectives:
- Walk through the recent quality regression observed in dedicated A/B on q4_0 quantized model (v2-prod -> v2-q4).
- Validate metrics & stat significance, align on immediate mitigations and experiments.
- Prioritize prompt set fixes vs model rollback vs post-processing heuristics.
Background / TL;DR:
- On 2026-02-28 we began a ramp of v2-q4 (to reduce token cost ~35%) across ~15% of traffic. After 48h we saw a measurable drop in the intent-extraction F1 for the refunds prompt-set.
- Summary numbers (quick):
  - Sample size: ~20,400 requests (randomized A/B, 50/50)
  - Baseline (v2-prod) intent-F1: 92.1%
  - v2-q4 observed intent-F1: 86.0% (delta -6.1pp)
  - A/B win-rate (user-level success metric): baseline 78.4% vs q4 73.1% (p~0.03)
  - Latency: median token-latency down ~12ms (expected)
- Note: other metrics (toxicity, repetition) largely unchanged in coarse aggregations.
Top failing prompt sets / slices (from eval harness):
- refunds-faq: failure modes -> truncated entity extraction, hallucinated policy references. Top example: expected "refund window 30 days" but q4 responded "refund within 7 days" (confidence low but surfaced in prod).
- billing-dispute: more partial answers, missing required clarifying question.
- edge-case slice: very long customer messages (>800 tokens) show higher drop-off (likely kv-cache precision/quant issues).
Hypotheses:
1) Quantization (q4_0) reduced logits precision causing token selection shifts in low-prob tails, leading to entity hallucination in narrow-domain prompts.
2) Specific tokens/positions in refunds prompt set rely on rare embeddings where fused-kernel selection deviates vs fp16.
3) Prompt formatting differences in the routed requests (runtime template) interact badly with caching and q4 fallback causing inconsistent prefix handling.
Quick checks to run (in prep):
- Re-run targeted evals locally on the same seed/samples with fp16/v2-q4 to reproduce numeric diffs (Aisha).
- Inspect top 100 mismatches, dump logits and per-token probs for both models (Jamie).
- Verify inference runtime config used in Dedicated pool for q4 rollout: batching/kv-cache settings, temperature, stop tokens (Lena).
- Run small controlled rerun with quantized model but with 0.0 temperature deterministic decode to isolate sampling vs token scoring (Matt).
Priority mitigation options (tradeoffs):
- Rollback v2-q4 from production immediately (fast, loses cost-savings) -> recommended if regression persists after sanity checks.
- Narrow the q4 rollout to non-sensitive routes (e.g., embeddings only) while keeping refunds on fp16 -> partial mitigation.
- Apply prompt-level guardrails: post-check entity extraction with deterministic regex fallback for refunds (engineering quick fix for high-criticality intents).
- Adjust compilation/kernel choices for q4 on problematic hardware (may require infra rollout, medium effort).
Action items (owner / ETA):
- Aisha: reproduce mismatch set with exact seeds + provide per-case diff CSV and top-20 examples (ETA 2026-03-05).
- Jamie: extract logits/prob traces for top 100 mismatches and upload to linked PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/reports/pull/234) (ETA 2026-03-05).
- Lena: confirm Dedicated pool runtime flags & rollout config; file small rollback plan and communication for SRE/CS (ETA 2026-03-04 EOD).
- Matt: run deterministic decode rerun (temp=0) and report whether disagreement persists (ETA 2026-03-05).
- Product/CS: flag affected customers (top 5 enterprise routes) and pre-draft communication (Jamie/Lena to coordinate) (ETA 2026-03-06).
Open questions / discussion points for 1:1 with Matt:
- How aggressive are we on cost targets vs tolerating small quality deltas? At what delta do we auto-rollback? (need firm SLO/guardrail policy)
- Do we have an automated metric-level monitoring that ties prompt-set regressions to rollouts? (we have evals infra but need alert thresholds)
- Should we expand eval prompt sets to include more of the refunds long-tail? What's the onboarding overhead?
Notes / misc: 
- Linked tickets: JIRA-EVALS-987 is tracking regression RCA; add new subtask under that for per-customer rollback comms.
- Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-OPTIMIZE-4821) to be updated with final keep/rollback decision and artifacts.
- Keep 1:1 focused on prioritization (rollback vs targeted fix) and owner sign-off for communication.
Meeting agenda (proposed, 20-25 min):
1) Quick recap & numbers (3m)
2) Walk top 5 failing cases (5-7m)
3) Review reproduce/check results from Aisha/Jamie (5-7m)
4) Decide mitigation & comms owner (5m)
5) Next steps and deadlines (2-3m)
Follow-ups after 1:1 (if decision = partial rollback):
- Draft rollback runbook and pre-approved message templates to CS (Lena)
- Prioritize prompt-set augmentation: add 500 more refunds examples to eval set (Product/QA)
- Schedule deeper infra/kernel perf test with release-eng (Engineering)
